action_items: (Cosmetic, non-blocking) Increase bar fill/visibility in MonteCarloCharts.jsx SuccessCompareChart — bars are nearly invisible against the white card background at the rendered scale.
critical_code_review_comments: MonteCarlo.jsx setAsset() does parseFloat(v)||0 — entering 0 legitimately is fine (||0 collapses NaN and 0 to 0). Acceptable.
MonteCarlo.jsx weightSum check uses Math.abs(weightSum - 1) > 0.001 — good tolerance for float rounding from /100.
api.js runMonteCarlo still polls 60×700ms = 42s. For larger n_trials this is tight; consider raising to ~60s or adding exponential backoff. Backend currently finishes <2s for n=1000, so non-urgent.

MonteCarlo.jsx res?.portfolio_mean / res?.portfolio_vol / res?.liquid_start are read without explicit null checks inside the JSX expression after `res &&` guard — safe today, but if backend ever omits these fields the fmtPct/fmtUSD helpers will print '—' rather than crash, which is the desired graceful behavior.
MonteCarlo.jsx mc-shock-years input clamps min via Math.max(1, ...) but the max={5} attribute is HTML-only and not enforced in onChange — a user can paste 99. Minor.

MonteCarlo.jsx — the 'success rate by X pts' delta uses (wc.success - nc.success)*100 with toFixed(1); when both are 0 you'd see '+0.0 pts' which is correct but the colorization still treats it as green via `>=`. Tiny edge case.
Per code review guideline: MonteCarlo.jsx is now ~265 lines, comfortably under the 700-line threshold. Good.
